newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian union says hungry nuclear workers may riot.
newsitem.headline: Russian union says hungry nuclear workers may riot.

text.p: A strike by hungry workers at a nuclear shipyard in Russia's far north could escalate into a riot unless they are quickly paid long-overdue wages, a local union leader was quoted as saying on Tuesday.

Alexander Usov told Itar-Tass news agency there had been cases of workers fainting from hunger or committing suicide at the firms attached to the shipyard in the town of Severodvinsk near the northern port of Arkhangelsk.
"Hungry people reduced to despair are capable of doing unpredictable things," Tass quoted him as saying.
"Such a state of affairs is impermissable at firms serving an atomic centre where potentially dangerous work with radioactive materials is being conducted," he added.
Usov said the government owed about 1.6 trillion roubles ($2.9 billion) to the companies and added that workers had not been paid their wages for up to eight months.
Some 12,000 unemployed workers had not received any state benefits for more than a year and pensioners had also not been paid for months, Usov said.

"All this has brought the town to the brink of catastrophe," he added. Power cuts were commonplace and the temperature in workplaces was virtually the same as outside on the frozen streets of the near-Arctic town.

Unpaid wages have become an acute problem across the vast Russian Federation in recent years affecting millions of workers including miners, teachers, doctors and the military as the government battles to revive the moribond economy.

The Kremlin blames tax-dodging by firms and individuals for the wage delays. Companies say they too are owed large sums of money, often by the government itself, which prevents them paying their taxes.
